prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a case where a clean theoretical prediction (Bistritzer and MacDonald, 2011) was followed by a decisive clue from nature (correlated insulators and superconductivity, 2018). That is the sequence I trust. The result has been reproduced by many independent groups and has opened moire and twistronics physics well beyond graphene, into transition-metal dichalcogenide systems and fractional Chern states. The discovery is clear and the theory-plus-experiment attribution is natural, with three names that fit the statutes. After reading the openings, eight of eight members ranked B042, with three first places, so it is the only candidate that every colleague regards as a serious contender. That is not merit, but the independent assessments of its originality and impact are consistent across the room.
statement.case_against: The field is only about eight years old after the key experiment, and the origin of the superconductivity is still debated; if the interpretation shifted substantially, an early prize would look hasty. Credit is also not airtight. Yuan Cao carried out the 2018 experiments as first author and is not among the three names, the earlier continuum-model work by Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto is outside the credited set, and other experimental groups (Dean, Young, Yazdani, Efetov) made decisive follow-ups. Optical lattice clocks (B012) are mature, quantitative and have the broadest first-place support among AMO-leaning members, and I would not be embarrassed if the committee preferred them.

responses.point: Optical lattice clocks (B012) are the clearest case of a new measurement technique reaching 1e-18 uncertainty, confirmed by several independent labs, with a natural two-name attribution of Katori and Ye, and timing made current by the possible redefinition of the second.
responses.response: I agree with the quality of the evidence and the cleanness of the attribution, and this is why B012 is my second choice. I disagree on novelty. The frequency comb was honoured in 2005 and ion clocks and single-quantum-system control in 2012, so the lattice clock is the third prize in one neighbourhood, an incremental step in precision. That does not make it unworthy, but it weighs against it when a new state of matter is available. I would also note that the redefinition of the second has not happened yet, so the claim that the application is complete is premature.

responses.point: Twisted bilayer graphene is a genuinely tunable new platform for correlated physics, but recognition may be slightly early because the superconductivity mechanism is unresolved, so interpretation is not yet stable; she ranked B012 first and B042 fourth.
responses.response: I take the maturity point seriously. I would answer that the Nobel Prize rewards the discovery, not the final theory of its mechanism. The flat-band prediction and the observation of the correlated insulators and the superconducting dome at the predicted angle are firm and widely reproduced, as for the cuprates, where the mechanism is still open decades later. Where I do concede is that twist-angle disorder and sample dependence were real concerns in the early years. Do you consider the reproduction in other moire systems, in particular the transition-metal dichalcogenides, enough to change your view that the principle is stable?

responses.point: Circuit QED (B005) gives the architecture on which essentially all superconducting processors run; the Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf split is natural, though Girvin is outside the names and she cautions about proximity to the 2025 prize.
responses.response: Circuit QED is a conceptually elegant and consequential advance, and I respect her caution about her own field. I share her worry about timing: the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is only one year behind us, and awarding another superconducting-circuit prize now would look unbalanced for the Academy. The attribution is also less clean than she suggests, since Girvin and Huang are part of the 2004 theory proposal and the transmon inventors are a separate claim. I would rank it below both B042 and B012 for this year.

responses.point: Magic-angle graphene is a clear case of a theoretically predicted flat-band condition realised experimentally with correlated insulators and superconductivity, and the Bistritzer-MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero pairing is natural; he ranked topological insulators (B030) third because credit is contested.
responses.response: We agree on B042, and I accept that Cao's omission and the broader experimental community remain open. On B030, I share his reservation. Kane and Mele are essential, but the HgTe prediction by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the three-dimensional work of Fu, Moore, Balents and Hasan leave a three-name allocation contested, and the 2016 prize already covers topological phases. I therefore keep B030 below the moire candidate.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept that the credited trio is the right allocation given the absence of Yuan Cao and the unresolved priority of Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto.
Whether the unresolved pairing mechanism makes the 2026 timing premature relative to the mature optical lattice clock candidate.
How much weight lattice clocks deserve after the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes, and whether a clock prize should be postponed until the redefinition of the second.
For the astrophysics candidate B016, whether the BeppoSAX team and the optical and radio followers, including the late van Paradijs, can be separated fairly with three names.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My PhD supervisor David Gross, my mentor Rubinstein and my co-author Van Riet are not candidates in any shortlisted entry, and my own field of string theory and cosmology is distant from all of these candidates.
